commits.title: The unsigned browser specs hold in a build that knows the Auth stand-in

changes.how: First find what fails. Locally: seed an empty database (node scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed), build once with the signed-in job's two variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3912 NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=e2e-publishable-key pnpm build), then run the unsigned projects against that build twice: once with the stand-in running (E2E_SIGNED_IN=1 pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium, which starts e2e/fixtures/auth-stub.mjs through the config's webServer list) and write down every failing test. Expected candidates: the health test here (lines 146 to 150 accept 200 or 503 because Supabase is not configured; with the stand-in it may answer 200 only, which the test already allows: leave it unless it fails), e2e/csp.spec.ts (the policy names the Supabase host) and the specs that test the admin 'without a session' (rg -l 'without a session|not configured|NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE' e2e --glob '*.spec.ts' lists ten: pages, admin, analytics-export, inline-edit-live, smoke, redirects-admin, data-export, replicate-probe, work, store-features-onboarding). For each failing test change only its expectation so that it holds in BOTH builds: where it asserted the exact text or status of 'Supabase is not configured', assert what both builds share (the visitor is sent to the sign-in page or gets 401/404 and sees no admin data). Never weaken a test to `expect(true)`, never skip one, never add a branch on an environment variable inside the app. If more than 15 tests fail, stop: the suites cannot share a build cheaply.

Only if it failed in the trial: where it expects the policy's connect-src without a Supabase host, make it accept the host of process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL when that variable is set in the test process. The policy itself (src/proxy.ts and docs/pci.md) does not change.

commits.title: The two browser suites share one build

changes.how: Decide the shape from numbers, not by taste. From the recorder of step 1.20 take the median of the last ten runs on main of: B = build-e2e seconds, E = e2e (the unsigned Playwright run), S = signed-in (the signed-in run), J_e2e and J_signed = the two jobs' whole durations, and SLOW = the longest whole duration among the jobs `release` needs (static, each integration shard, e2e, hosts, signed-in, audit). SHAPE A (one job) is allowed only if J_e2e + S <= SLOW and J_e2e + S <= 600 seconds. Then: delete job `signed-in`; rename nothing else; in job `e2e` add to `env` the three variables of the signed-in job (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:3912, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: e2e-publishable-key, E2E_SIGNED_IN: "1"), keep its steps, and make the test step run every project (`pnpm test:e2e`, which with E2E_SIGNED_IN runs chromium, webkit, signed-in-setup and signed-in); keep one failure-artifact step. In `release` remove signed-in from `needs` and from the `if`. SHAPE B (one build, two test jobs) otherwise. A build cannot simply be handed to another job: the storefront is prerendered from the database, and scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed gives every row a new random id (the seed has no fixed ids), so a build made on one job's database does not match another job's. Shape B therefore hands over the build AND the database: add a job `browser-build` (same container image, same postgres service, the signed-in job's two NEXT_PUBLIC variables) with steps install, seed, `pnpm build`, then a dump of the seeded database to one SQL file and a save of `.next` (without `.next/cache`) and that file with actions/cache/save under the key `browser-build-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}`. Use actions/cache, not upload-artifact: artifact storage is metered on a private repository's free plan, the cache is free up to 10 GB and evicts by itself. The dump needs a pg_dump of the server's major version (17) inside the job; the Playwright image has none. Write the dump with a small Node script instead (scripts/e2e-db.mjs, see the next entry). Jobs `e2e` and `signed-in` then get `needs: [browser-build]`, drop their `pnpm build` step, restore the cache with actions/cache/restore and `fail-on-cache-miss: true`, load the database from the file instead of seeding, and run their tests as today (e2e gets the two NEXT_PUBLIC variables in its env so the server starts as it was built). `release` adds browser-build to `needs` and to its `if`. If the chain (browser-build's whole duration + the longer test job) comes out above SLOW on the first three runs, split the unsigned run in two with a matrix `shard: [1, 2]` and `pnpm test:e2e --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/2`; if it is still above SLOW, revert this commit and report: the step's own rule (no slower) wins over two builds. In the same commit, in scripts/ci-budgets.json (made by step 1.20): remove the keys of labels that no longer exist (build-signed-in, and signed-in in shape A) and add the new labels with no ceiling; they are filled from the median of the next ten runs as step 1.20's rule says. Never raise an existing ceiling.

Only for shape B. Plain Node with the `postgres` package the repo already has. `node scripts/e2e-db.mjs save <file>`: for every table of schema commerce (and any other schema the seed writes: list them with select table_schema, table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema not in ('pg_catalog','information_schema')), in foreign-key-safe order or with `set session_replication_role = replica`, write the rows as JSON lines keyed by table, leaving out generated columns (information_schema.columns.is_generated = 'ALWAYS'), and write every sequence's last value. `node scripts/e2e-db.mjs load <file>`: on a database that has just had `node scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed` run (so the schema, functions and triggers exist), inside one transaction with `set local session_replication_role = replica`: truncate the same tables, insert the saved rows with `insert into t select * from jsonb_populate_recordset(null::t, $1)` naming the non-generated columns, and setval the sequences. End by comparing row counts per table with the file and exit 1 on a difference. Add a unit-free check to the workflow: after load, `select count(*) from commerce.products` equals the file's count. This script is used by CI only; say so in its header and that it refuses a DATABASE_URL whose host is not localhost, 127.0.0.1 or postgres.

Add a test `the app is built in two CI jobs`: the jobs of ci.yml whose text contains a `pnpm build` command are exactly ["e2e", "hosts"] (shape A) or ["browser-build", "hosts"] (shape B), and no job with a `strategy: matrix` contains `pnpm build` (a matrix would build once per shard). Add: every job that runs Playwright (`playwright test` or `pnpm test:e2e`) is in `release`'s `needs` list and named in its `if`.

Lines 29 to 40 expect at least four image tags and the browser jobs ["e2e", "hosts", "scan", "signed-in"]. Shape A: at least three tags and ["e2e", "hosts", "scan"]. Shape B: add "browser-build" only if it runs `playwright install` (it should not). Change nothing else in the test.

do_not: Do not use a paid runner, a larger runner or paid artifact storage. Use actions/cache for the handed-over build.
Do not merge or change the hosts job: its build differs (NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_DOMAIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_THEMES_HOST, NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_HOST).
Do not add a sign-in bypass or a test-only branch to the app: the Auth stand-in is the only fake (CLAUDE.md).
Do not put pnpm build under a matrix: each shard would build, and the count of two would be true only on paper.
Do not hand a build to a job that seeds its own database: the prerendered pages carry the build database's ids.
Do not remove a job from release's needs without adding its replacement, and do not touch the migration or deploy steps of pending, release, redeploy or baseline.
Do not move the skip of a deploy for a tests-only push here: that is step 0.38's.
Do not skip, delete or loosen a spec to make the shared build pass.
stop_if: More than 15 unsigned tests fail in the build that knows the Auth stand-in.
scripts/timed.mjs or its recorded timings do not exist (step 1.20 is not done): there is no before figure to compare with.
Shape B's database load does not give the same row counts, or any spec fails that passed before with the job's own seed.
After the shard rule the slowest job release waits for is still slower than before, or a run passes 10 minutes: revert the third commit and report the numbers.
A push to main ran neither lint nor the type check (both steps skipped in both jobs): revert the second commit at once.
executor_why: The third commit is a choice between two CI shapes made from measured seconds, and the second shape must move a seeded database between jobs; a wrong CI change shows only on real runs and can hold back a release.
checked_in_code: I read .github/workflows/ci.yml (static line 43, e2e 116, hosts 170, signed-in 215, pending 273, release 338), playwright.config.ts, src/lib/ci-playwright.scan.test.ts, e2e/smoke.spec.ts and supabase/seed.sql. The finding's facts hold: three jobs run pnpm build, the e2e and signed-in builds differ only in two NEXT_PUBLIC variables, and E2E_SIGNED_IN is read by the Playwright config alone. Two corrections. The plan's fallback (keep two test jobs and hand them one build as an artifact) cannot work as written: the build prerenders from the database and the seed gives new random ids each time, so the database must travel with the build; the brief adds that and uses the free Actions cache, not metered artifact storage. Lint and the type check run twice only on pushes where the quick gate runs, so the fix is a pair of complementary conditions on static and pending, not the removal of a job. src/lib/ci-once.scan.test.ts and scripts/timed.mjs do not exist yet (steps 0.38 and 1.20 make them).
